edition.title: Cyber — Saturday, 31 October 2026
edition.lead: Binance says about $6.3 billion was drained from its wallets on 29 Oct, and two blockchain firms, TRM and Chainalysis, tie the theft to North Korea's TraderTraitor; Binance has not confirmed that attribution.
gaps: web_extract was unavailable (search-only backend), so stories rest on search snippets and secondary reports; primary pages were not read in full.
I could not read the middle of the previous edition, so thread keys for Binance, Ivanti, CVE-2026-98432, Claude Code and UEFI are new and may repeat earlier coverage. The PHP2Shell key is inferred.
CVE-2026-98432: Ubuntu's fix status is unresolved. Ubuntu's CVE page was only a search snippet, and secondary reports conflict.
Ivanti fixed-version thresholds for the 25.1.3 line differ between sources; Ivanti's advisory was not read directly.
CSIRT Chile's listing I could read ends 23 Oct; I found no Chile or ANCI alerts for 24-31 Oct.
Binance attribution rests on TRM, Chainalysis and Elliptic; there is no Binance root-cause report or law-enforcement statement in my sources.
Trezor's implant is unverified (device not examined). The ARTEX outcome figures (140 vs nine organizations) are not reconciled, and CrowdStrike's report was read only as a snippet.
No Dell advisory for CVE-2026-97631 was found, so the OptiPlex 3080 status is unverified. Mitigation advice for CVE-2026-98432 conflicts across sources; I tested none of it.

stories.headline: Ivanti Connect Secure: CISA adds CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527 to KEV, completing a root-escalation chain
stories.summary: On 30 Oct 2026 CISA added CVE-2026-111357 (privilege escalation to root) and CVE-2026-118527 (arbitrary file write) to KEV. Both are links in a chain with CVE-2026-104935, an authentication bypass that CISA added on 13 Oct. Ivanti says it knows of limited exploitation of the chain. CISA says attackers use it for credential theft and data exfiltration, and cites the Volexity analysis.
stories.action: Upgrade Connect Secure to 25.1.1.3 or 22.8R2.6, or the later fixed build in Ivanti's advisory. If the appliance was reachable from the internet before you patched, treat it as possibly compromised and follow Ivanti's recovery steps: back up the configuration, factory reset and rebuild, restore, reset all account passwords, and reissue certificates.

details.label: Who's affected
details.text: Ivanti Connect Secure 25.1.1.2 and earlier, 25.1.2.2 and earlier, and 22.8R2.5 and earlier (per CISA).

details.label: Status
details.text: Confirmed exploited (CISA KEV, 30 Oct). Fixed builds 25.1.1.3 and 22.8R2.6 per the Canadian Cyber Centre and CCB Belgium. Red Tiger Security says 25.1.3.0 and later are clean, while the Canadian Cyber Centre lists 25.1.3.1 as the threshold; check Ivanti's advisory for the 25.1.3 line.

details.label: Next
details.text: Connect Secure 22.8 reaches end of life on 31 Jan 2027, per Ivanti and CISA.

stories.headline: PHP2Shell: Palo Alto confirms active exploitation against PAN-OS management interfaces, with a root chain
stories.summary: On 29 Oct Palo Alto Networks, through Unit 42, said attackers are actively exploiting PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) against PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to the internet. Unit 42 says it independently verified attacker tools that combine the PHP flaws with a Linux kernel vulnerability to reach root. Press reports, citing Dream's research, say about 25 servers were rooted, including US government-affiliated firewalls; I did not verify that count. A secondary write-up links the kernel half to Fragnesia (CVE-2026-46300).
stories.action: If PAN-OS management is reachable from the internet, restrict it to internal networks now and apply the fixed PAN-OS release in Palo Alto's advisory (version not read here). Update PHP to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35; PHP 8.1 and earlier have no official support, so migrate or get vendor patches, per ANCI. Confirm the kernel carries the fix for CVE-2026-46300.

details.label: Who's affected
details.text: PAN-OS firewalls with internet-exposed management interfaces. PHP servers using PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP or LiteSpeed, per ANCI.

details.label: Status
details.text: Vendor-confirmed active exploitation (Palo Alto, 29 Oct). The 25-server figure is press-reported; attacks began about 23 Oct per press.

details.label: Next
details.text: Palo Alto's advisory names the fixed PAN-OS versions; I did not read it.

framing.text: Press reports attribute the campaign to a suspected China-linked crew; I did not find that attribution in Palo Alto's note.

stories.headline: Binance's $6.3B theft: TRM and Chainalysis tie it to North Korea's TraderTraitor; Binance reserves $6.34B to cover losses
stories.summary: Binance said about $6.3 billion was impacted and, with blockchain partners, froze roughly $3 billion. TRM says the attacker moved about $6.36 billion from Binance wallets on ten blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes on 29 Oct, and rates the TraderTraitor link high confidence. Chainalysis says likely. Wired reports Binance has said the attack began with a compromised engineer's laptop. Neither Binance nor law enforcement has named a suspect.

details.label: Who's affected
details.text: Binance hot wallets across ten blockchains, including Ethereum, Bitcoin, Tron and Solana. Binance says it will cover losses.

details.label: Status
details.text: Deposits and withdrawals were suspended after the theft (Wired). On Friday 30 Oct Binance said it had reserved more than $6.34 billion to cover losses (The Hill).

framing.text: TRM rates the North Korea link high confidence and says preparation began at least 36 hours before the theft; Chainalysis says likely.
Wired reports that neither Binance nor law enforcement has named any suspected link to North Korea.

stories.blindspot: No Binance root-cause report or law-enforcement statement appears in my sources; the attribution rests on analytics firms.

stories.headline: Java and eMudhra: Oracle's 24 Oct follow-up CVE-2026-114820 is missing from the CSIRT Chile alerts I could read
stories.summary: CSIRT Nacional issued AVC26-00742 (eMudhra intermediate keys) and AVC26-00745 (Java CVE-2026-91403, CVSS 9.1) on 22 Oct. Oracle's follow-up, CVE-2026-114820 (CVSS 9.1, published 24 Oct), covers Java builds that carried the first fix, including 21.0.13.0.2 and 17.0.21.0.2, and removes more eMudhra and Comodo roots from cacerts. I found no CSIRT alert for CVE-2026-114820. The CSIRT listing I could read ends on 23 Oct, and a Chilean analysis says no alert had been issued when it was written.
stories.action: Java: move to 21.0.13.0.3, 17.0.21.0.3, 11.0.33.0.3 or 1.8.0_511-b33, the baseline in a Chilean analysis; confirm against Oracle's advisory. Then run keytool -list -cacerts | grep -i emsign and expect no output. Python: upgrade certifi; the same analysis says version 2026.10.18 dropped the emSign roots. Go binaries you build: rebuild with Go 1.26.10 or 1.27.3, which block the affected intermediates (CVE-2026-111943).

details.label: Who's affected
details.text: Java SE, GraalVM and Java-embedded products on the affected builds. Go and Python tools that ship their own trust store also trust the eMudhra chain unless updated.
